scores.evidence: Retries: at most 2, with jittered backoff, only on 429 and 5xx responses.
scores.rationale: Mechanisms (RRF, SKIP LOCKED outbox, hybrid search, idempotent tickets) are correct and the plan flags unpublish gaps in incremental feeds; minor issues like regex-only redaction and the unpublish-latency gap keep it from 4.

scores.evidence: Non-goals (for this plan): Account-specific actions or lookups (order status, refunds, password resets).
scores.rationale: Solves the actual request, resolves ambiguity with stated defaults, separates essentials from deferred items with explicit reasons and triggers, and is clearly buildable by a small team.

scores.evidence: Handoffs are written to an outbox table in the same transaction as the turn. The Handoff Worker sends them to the ticketing system and retries until they succeed.
scores.rationale: Component responsibilities, data ownership, and flows are consistent, with choices like public-only index, validation-before-display and no-streaming honored throughout; minor loose ends only (e.g., 'handoff_offered' route naming).

scores.evidence: Judge calibration: agrees with SME grades on 50 cases at least 85% of the time. If it doesn't, adjust the rubric before trusting it.
scores.rationale: Risk-specific validation: frozen eval set early in M1, CI regression gates, spikes with change-the-plan thresholds, fault injection, nightly live eval, holdout; targets are labeled as assumptions.

scores.evidence: | A2 | Zendesk Guide and Zendesk Support | Connector and handoff code change (about 3–5 days each).
scores.rationale: Assumption table with impact if wrong and validation timing, defaults for open questions, and targets explicitly marked as provisional.

scores.rationale: Covers unpublish staleness, LLM timeout, ticketing outage with idempotency and duplicates, injection, XSS links, denial of wallet, card data, with detection, alerts and recovery runbooks.

scores.evidence: On-call during business hours only, because the failure mode is falling back to the contact form.
scores.rationale: Metrics, alerts with runbooks, kill switch, staged rollout and rollback, migrations, ownership and weekly review sized to a small team.

scores.evidence: 120k turns works out to roughly $1–2.5k on a mid-tier model, or roughly $300–600 on a small one.
scores.rationale: Dominant driver (LLM tokens) estimated with basis, controls (spend cap, history cap, model tier), and build-vs-buy noted; people cost is less quantified and the $0.10 target is somewhat loosely grounded.

scores.evidence: Easy to extend later. Leaking content is not reversible.
scores.rationale: Each decision has reversibility and revisit triggers, gateway isolates model/vendor, embedding model column enables migration, build-vs-buy spiked early.

scores.evidence: One structured LLM call per turn returns structured output... No agent loop and no tools beyond "create a ticket".
scores.rationale: Starts with simplest design (one Postgres, no vector DB, no agent, no reranker until measured) with deferrals and triggers; outbox and eval harness are warranted.

scores.evidence: Done when | Merging to main deploys automatically. The staging `/healthz` returns 200 including the database check.
scores.rationale: Task breakdown with dependencies, repo layout, checkable done-criteria, critical path, time-boxed spikes with change-the-plan conditions.

checklist.evidence: Every 15 minutes: incremental fetch since the last cursor... Nightly: a full listing to reconcile. Articles that disappeared, were unpublished... marked `deleted`
Split on H2/H3 headings into 300–600 tokens. Prefix each chunk with `Article title > Section path`.
Evaluation suite on the frozen corpus | CI on AI-path pull requests, plus nightly against the live index
`route=answer` needs at least one citation, and every citation must be one of the retrieved source IDs.
A keyword list goes straight to `handoff` without calling the LLM: "cancel my account", "chargeback", "legal", "speak to a human"
No privileged tools. Retrieved text sits inside source tags... 25 or more adversarial evaluation cases.
Only articles visible to anonymous visitors get indexed. Restricted and internal content is out of the index entirely.
Transcripts, turns and feedback: 90 days [A7], then deleted by a nightly job.
Account-specific actions or lookups (order status, refunds, password resets).
Weekly quality review: a sample of 50 thumbs-down and 50 random turns, graded by the SME. Failures are added to the evaluation set.
Controls: the daily spend cap, cost recorded per turn, history capped at the last 4 turns

traps.evidence: If there's no valid citation, the bot doesn't answer and offers a human instead.
Filter on visibility at ingestion. Fixture test with a restricted article.
Evaluation suite on the frozen corpus | CI on AI-path pull requests
Whether to add a reranker or retrieve whole articles is settled by spike S1, not assumed.

note: Exceptionally thorough, well-proportioned plan with eval-first approach, explicit assumptions, grounded validated answers; main weaknesses are public-only index deferring entitlement filtering and lightly handled PII/regional specifics.
